- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
2	## Rental Management System for IT Equipment Rental Services
3	
4	**Version:** 1.0  
5	**Date:** 2026-07-02  
6	**Prepared For:** Rental Services Business  
7	**Prepared By:** Claude Code  
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Table of Contents
12	1. [Introduction](#1-introduction)
13	   - 1.1 Purpose
14	   - 1.2 Scope
15	   - 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
16	   - 1.4 References
17	   - 1.5 Overview
18	2. [Overall Description](#2-overall-description)
19	   - 2.1 Product Perspective
20	   - 2.2 Product Functions
21	   - 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
22	   - 2.4 Operating Environment
23	   - 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
24	   - 2.6 User Documentation
25	   - 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
26	3. [Specific Requirements](#3-specific-requirements)
27	   - 3.1 External Interface Requirements
28	   - 3.2 Functional Requirements
29	   - 3.3 Non-Functional Requirements
30	   - 3.4 Other Requirements
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. Introduction
35	
36	### 1.1 Purpose
37	This document specifies the software requirements for a Rental Management System (RMS) designed specifically for an IT equipment rental services business. The system will manage the rental operations for servers, laptops, computers, firewalls, printers, and refurbished IT equipment serving business customers including IT companies, manufacturing firms, startups, educational institutions, and BPOs/call centers.
38	
39	### 1.2 Scope
40	The Rental Management System will provide:
41	- Inventory management for all rental equipment
42	- Customer and contract management
43	- Rental transaction processing
44	- Billing and invoicing
45	- Maintenance and repair tracking
46	- Reporting and analytics
47	- Integration with the existing customer-facing website
48	- User role-based access control
49	
50	The system will **not** serve individual consumers; it is strictly for business-to-business (B2B) transactions.
51	
52	### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
53	
54	| Term | Definition |
55	|------|------------|
56	| RMS | Rental Management System |
57	| B2B | Business-to-Business |
58	| CRM | Customer Relationship Management |
59	| ERP | Enterprise Resource Planning |
60	| SLA | Service Level Agreement |
61	| OEM | Original Equipment Manufacturer |
62	| SLA | Service Level Agreement |
63	
64	### 1.4 References
65	- [IEEE 830-1998] IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications
66	- Existing website: `index.html`, `style.css`, `main.js`
67	- Brand assets: `icons/` directory containing brand logos
68	
69	### 1.5 Overview
70	The remainder of this document describes the overall description of the product (Section 2) and the specific requirements (Section 3) including external interfaces, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and other requirements.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 2. Overall Description
75	
76	### 2.1 Product Perspective
77	The Rental Management System is a web-based application designed to operate as the backend system for the rental services business. It will integrate with the existing customer-facing website (currently at `index.html`) to provide real-time inventory availability, rental requests, and customer account management.
78	
79	The system will be a multi-user application accessible via web browsers, with different interfaces for administrators, staff, and customers (via portal access).
80	
81	### 2.2 Product Functions
82	The RMS will provide the following core functions:
83	1. **Inventory Management** - Track all rental equipment by type, brand, model, serial number, condition, and availability
84	2. **Customer Management** - Maintain B2B customer profiles, contact information, rental history, and credit terms
85	3. **Rental Management** - Handle rental requests, quotations, contracts, equipment allocation, pickup/delivery scheduling, and returns
86	4. **Billing and Invoicing** - Generate invoices, process payments, track overdue payments, and manage security deposits
87	5. **Maintenance Management** - Track equipment maintenance, repairs, servicing schedules, and warranty claims
88	6. **Reporting and Analytics** - Generate reports on utilization, revenue, customer analytics, and inventory performance
89	7. **Customer Portal** - Allow customers to browse inventory, request rentals, view active rentals, and make payments
90	8. **Integration** - Synchronize with the existing website to display real-time availability and product information
91	
92	### 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
93	
94	| User Type | Characteristics | Permissions |
95	|-----------|----------------|-------------|
96	| **System Administrator** | IT staff responsible for system configuration, user management, and system maintenance | Full system access including user management, system configuration, and all business functions |
97	| **Rental Manager** | Business users managing rental operations, inventory, and customer relationships | Full access to rental, inventory, customer, and billing functions; limited system administration |
98	| **Sales Representative** | Staff handling customer inquiries, quotations, and rental agreements | Access to customer management, rental quotations, and contract creation |
99	| **Operations Staff** | Personnel handling equipment preparation, delivery, pickup, and maintenance | Access to inventory management, equipment status updates, and maintenance scheduling |
100	| **Accounting/Finance** | Staff handling invoicing, payments, and financial reporting | Access to billing, invoicing, payment processing, and financial reports |
101	| **Customer Portal User** | Authorized representatives from B2B customers | Browse inventory, submit rental requests, view active rentals, download invoices, and make payments |
102	
103	### 2.4 Operating Environment
104	- **Web Application:** Browser-based interface accessible via modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
105	- **Deployment:** Web server (Apache/Nginx) with application server (Node.js/PHP/Python)
106	- **Database:** Relational database (MySQL/PostgreSQL/MariaDB)
107	- **Integration:** RESTful API for integration with existing website
108	- **Security:** HTTPS encryption, role-based access control, input validation
109	- **Compatibility:** Responsive design for desktop and tablet use
110	
111	### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
112	1. **Integration Constraint:** Must integrate seamlessly with the existing website at `index.html`
113	2. **Technology Stack:** Should leverage existing web technologies where possible (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript)
114	3. **Data Migration:** Must accommodate import of existing inventory and customer data
115	4. **Brand Compliance:** Must comply with brand guidelines for all displayed OEM logos and product information
116	5. **Business Rules:** Must enforce B2B-only rental policy (no individual consumers)
117	6. **Regulatory:** Must comply with data protection regulations for customer information
118	
119	### 2.6 User Documentation
120	- Administrator Guide
121	- Staff User Manual
122	- Customer Portal Guide
123	- API Documentation for website integration
124	- Troubleshooting FAQ
125	
126	### 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
127	1. The existing website will remain as the primary customer-facing interface
128	2. The RMS will provide APIs for the website to consume inventory and rental data
129	3. All customers are verified business entities (no individual consumers)
130	4. Initial inventory data will be migrated from existing records
131	5. The system will operate in a single timezone (IST - India Standard Time)
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 3. Specific Requirements
136	
137	### 3.1 External Interface Requirements
138	
139	#### 3.1.1 User Interfaces
140	- **Administrator Dashboard:** Web-based interface for system configuration and oversight
141	- **Staff Interface:** Web-based interface for rental operations, inventory management, and customer service
142	- **Customer Portal:** Secure web interface for customers to browse inventory, request rentals, and manage accounts
143	- **Responsive Design:** All interfaces must be responsive and accessible on desktop and tablet devices
144	- **Brand Consistency:** UI must align with the visual identity of the existing website
145	
146	#### 3.1.2 Hardware Interfaces
147	- Barcode/RFID scanners for inventory tracking (optional)
148	- Receipt printers for on-site transactions
149	- Signature capture devices for delivery confirmations (optional)
150	
151	#### 3.1.3 Software Interfaces
152	- **RESTful API:** For integration with the existing website to provide:
153	  - Real-time inventory availability
154	  - Product catalog information
155	  - Rental request submission
156	  - Customer account information (read-only for website)
157	- **Database:** MySQL 8.0+ or PostgreSQL 12+
158	- **Authentication:** Integration with LDAP/Active Directory optional for internal users
159	- **Payment Gateway:** Integration with payment processors (Stripe, Razorpay, PayPal) for online payments
160	- **Email Service:** Integration with SMTP service for automated notifications (SendGrid, AWS SES, etc.)
161	
162	#### 3.1.4 Communications Interfaces
163	- HTTP/HTTPS for web interfaces
164	- REST/JSON for API communications
165	- SMTP for email notifications
166	- SMS gateway integration optional for SMS notifications
167
